sections.heading: Core Gameplay Mechanics
sections.body:
In Elite MiniGolf, the core gameplay mechanics are centered around precision and control. Players use their mouse, keyboard, or touch controls to aim, putt, and control their shots. The game features a variety of shot types, including putts, drives, and chips, each with its unique characteristics and challenges. As players progress through the game, they'll encounter a range of obstacles, including sand traps, water hazards, and challenging terrain. The game's physics engine is impressively realistic, with shots behaving as they would in real-life golf.

One of the key features of Elite MiniGolf is its shot control system. Players can use a variety of controls to manipulate their shots, including power, trajectory, and spin. The game also features a shot meter, which helps players gauge their shot's speed, distance, and accuracy. With practice and patience, players can master the art of controlling their shots and achieve the coveted hole-in-one. But what makes Elite MiniGolf truly challenging is its ability to adapt to the player's skill level. Throughout the game, players will encounter a range of power-ups and bonuses that can help them overcome obstacles and achieve better scores. These power-ups include speed boosts, shot modifiers, and obstacles that can be used to hinder opponents. Players can also collect coins and rewards to upgrade their equipment and unlock new courses and features. With its engaging gameplay mechanics and addictive features, Elite MiniGolf is a game that will keep you hooked from start to finish.
